_readme: Form A rubric eval. One entry per moment: Sunny's /label ground truth (labels.json) plus 4 frozen player answers with hand grades (correct, missing-details, incorrect, vague). Answers were written and graded by Claude against Sunny's labels. scripts/eval_rubric.ts extracts claims with Haiku, scores with src/lib/review/rubric.ts, and reports agreement with `expected`.

label.idea: cover the bishop, attack g7 pawn, give queen diagonal space
label.opponentMotif: Trade knight for bishop and attack weakened king

answers.answer: Qg3: the queen keeps covering the bishop on d3 and attacks the g7 pawn along the diagonal. Otherwise Black trades the knight on e5 for my bishop and goes after my king on c1.
Queen to g3, it protects the bishop and hits g7.
Push e5 to kick the knight on f6 and open lines.
Just move the queen somewhere safe.
White threatens Bb5+, forking my king on e8 and my rook on a4. Ke7 gets the king off that diagonal so I don't get forked.
Move the king to e7 so I don't walk into a fork.
Trade bishops with Bd4 to simplify.
Something about my rook being loose.

label.idea: capture pawn, prevent castling, and fork the bishop.
label.opponentMotif: opponent easily defends and develops, up material

answers.answer: Bxf7+ takes the pawn and the king can't castle anymore, then Qd5+ forks the king and the bishop on c5. If I don't, Black just develops and stays a pawn up.
Sacrifice the bishop on f7 with check and then fork with the queen.
Recapture the pawn with bxc3.
Attack the king.

label.idea: Threaten checkmate, Force opponent into repeatedly checking me

answers.answer: Ra8 threatens Rh8 mate, so Black has to keep checking me with the rook from a1 instead of promoting the a2 pawn.
Rook to a8 to threaten mate on h8.
Take the g7 pawn with the rook.
Stop the a-pawn from queening.

label.idea: Taking the opponent's pawn and moving your rook out of skewer danger

answers.answer: Rxg5 grabs the pawn and gets my rook off g8, because Rd8+ checks my king on f8 and then skewers and wins the rook on g8.
Take the g5 pawn with the rook.
Move the king to e7 to centralize it.
Take the b2 pawn.

label.idea: get the knight out of trouble and toward more important places
label.opponentMotif: threaten to checkmate me and my knight still in danger

answers.answer: The knight on g6 is in trouble, so Ne5 gets it out and heads toward c6. Meanwhile Black is threatening mate on my king on c1 with Rb8.
Save the knight with Ne5.
Push f4 to support g5 and keep attacking the king.
Defend my king.

label.idea: Pawn break: create something on the other side of the board

answers.answer: a4 is a pawn break on the queenside against b5, creating play on the other side before Black's own pawn break on the kingside with f3 comes first.
Open the queenside with a pawn break.
Kc2 to tuck the king away safely.
Improve my pieces.

label.idea: Take initiative taking space in the center.

answers.answer: Push d5 to grab space in the center and take the initiative, because otherwise Black plays Bxc4 and cxd4 and takes my center pawns.
d5, gain space in the center.
Qb3 to protect the c4 pawn and use the b-file.
Put the rook on e1.
